item.text:
Current index items remain in force; I am not repeating them. The follow-up below only adds the pieces that materially narrow the two open 8B gaps.

**Gap Status**
- Independent outcome audits for flagship programs: partly resolved.
- Attribution versus inherited conditions and external shocks: partly resolved.

**New Evidence**
- AIFA audit findings show the rollout was not clean or fully controlled.
SOURCE_CLAIM_JSON: {"title":"Conoce las observaciones que la ASF hizo al AIFA","publisher":"A21","publication_date":"2022-02-22","url":"https://a21.com.mx/aeropuertos/2022/02/22/conoce-las-observaciones-que-la-asf-hizo-al-aifa-2/","claim":"ASF reported nine irregularities in the AIFA construction audits, including payments without documentation, uncredited materials, missing project and budget documentation, and other execution gaps across a 17,006 million peso sample.","locator":"lines 52-68","source_type":"media","source_confidence":"medium_high","source_confidence_reason":"Secondary reporting that directly quotes and summarizes the ASF's audit findings with concrete numeric detail.","final_evidence_use":"final_evidence","period_fit":"Directly within 2022 and tied to construction executed under AMLO's program.","ruler_attribution":"Directly attributable to AMLO's flagship project implementation through the federal security/transport apparatus, though the audit concerns construction management rather than personal conduct.","contrary_evidence":["Audit observations are not final judicial findings and may be partially clarified later."],"lenses":["8B.6","8B.8","8B.10"]}

- AIFA opened, but early utilization was very low.
SOURCE_CLAIM_JSON: {"title":"AIFA transportó a 13 mil 716 pasajeros en marzo; Cancún la ruta más solicitada","publisher":"Infobae","publication_date":"2022-04-27","url":"https://www.infobae.com/america/mexico/2022/04/27/aifa-transporto-a-13-mil-716-pasajeros-en-marzo-cancun-la-ruta-mas-solicitada/","claim":"AIFA carried 13,716 passengers in March 2022, with 67 departures and 66 arrivals, indicating very low early utilization after opening.","locator":"opening paragraphs on passenger totals and flights","source_type":"media","source_confidence":"medium_high","source_confidence_reason":"Reporting cites AFAC traffic figures and gives a concrete early utilization snapshot.","final_evidence_use":"final_evidence","period_fit":"Directly within the target year, immediately after the March 21 opening.","ruler_attribution":"Attributable to AMLO's flagship airport project and its early operational uptake; low traffic reflects demand and airline relocation constraints as well as design choices.","contrary_evidence":["A new airport's first month is a ramp-up period, so this is an early implementation outcome rather than final performance."],"lenses":["8B.6","8B.7","8B.10"]}

- Dos Bocas shows major execution slippage and cost escalation.
SOURCE_CLAIM_JSON: {"title":"Mexico's Pemex requests $6.5 billion more funding for 'Dos Bocas' refinery -documents, source","publisher":"Reuters","publication_date":"2022-08-12","url":"https://m.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/mexicos-pemex-requests-65-billion-more-funding-for-dos-bocas-refinery--documents-source-2871661?ampMode=1","claim":"Pemex requested almost $6.5 billion more for Dos Bocas, pushing the refinery's projected cost to $14.6 billion, far above the original $8.9 billion budget, because of works not initially included and higher construction/startup costs.","locator":"lines 12-18 and 24-28","source_type":"media","source_confidence":"high","source_confidence_reason":"Reuters reporting based on a document and multiple sources, with specific figures and budget comparisons.","final_evidence_use":"final_evidence","period_fit":"Directly within 2022.","ruler_attribution":"Directly attributable to AMLO's signature energy project and the administration's execution choices, though higher costs also reflect project complexity and inflation.","contrary_evidence":["Cost escalation does not prove failure on its own; it does show serious budget pressure and incomplete initial planning."],"lenses":["8B.2","8B.6","8B.7","8B.10"]}

- La Escuela es Nuestra still had weak supervision and documentation.
SOURCE_CLAIM_JSON: {"title":"La ASF detecta 573 mdp 'perdidos' en el programa La Escuela es Nuestra","publisher":"Expansión Política","publication_date":"2022-03-03","url":"https://politica.expansion.mx/mexico/2022/03/03/asf-irregularidades-escuela-es-nuestra","claim":"The ASF reported more than 573 million pesos in unresolved observations for La Escuela es Nuestra, including missing documentation, lack of proof of use of support funds, and the absence of periodic monitoring, supervision, and evaluation mechanisms.","locator":"lines 74-119","source_type":"media","source_confidence":"high","source_confidence_reason":"Secondary reporting that quotes and summarizes the ASF audit findings in detail, with specific amounts and mechanism failures.","final_evidence_use":"final_evidence","period_fit":"Directly within 2022, reviewing the program's 2020 operation and 2022 continuation.","ruler_attribution":"Directly attributable to AMLO's education policy design and rollout through SEP, though the audit concerns program controls rather than intent.","contrary_evidence":["The article also notes that the predecessor schools-of-full-day model had positive learning findings, so the policy choice was a tradeoff rather than a blank failure."],"lenses":["8B.2","8B.5","8B.6","8B.8","8B.10"]}

- UNICEF saw real, if limited, learning-recovery gains from government-led work.
SOURCE_CLAIM_JSON: {"title":"Teaching at the Right Level supports learning recovery in Mexico","publisher":"UNICEF","publication_date":"2022-03-01","url":"https://www.unicef.org/documents/teaching-right-level-supports-learning-recovery-mexico","claim":"Mexico's Ministry of Education, with UNICEF and partners, used government-led Learning Camps to close foundational learning gaps, reaching thousands of children with targeted literacy and numeracy instruction and showing measurable gains in weeks.","locator":"About section, lines 197-198","source_type":"IGO","source_confidence":"high","source_confidence_reason":"UNICEF case study with concrete implementation and outcome language, albeit focused on a targeted intervention rather than the entire system.","final_evidence_use":"final_evidence","period_fit":"Directly within 2022.","ruler_attribution":"Partly attributable to AMLO's education ministry and its recovery strategy, though UNICEF and partners share implementation and the case study is not a national average.","contrary_evidence":["This is a case study of a targeted intervention, not a full audit of national learning outcomes."],"lenses":["8B.6","8B.7","8B.8","8B.10"]}

- IMF macro review separates policy choices from shocks better than the raw outcome indicators alone.
SOURCE_CLAIM_JSON: {"title":"IMF Executive Board Concludes 2022 Article IV Consultation with Mexico","publisher":"International Monetary Fund","publication_date":"2022-11-04","url":"https://www.imf.org/en/news/articles/2022/11/04/pr22373-imf-executive-board-concludes-2022-article-iv-consultation-with-mexico","claim":"The IMF said Mexico's recovery accelerated in the first half of 2022 due to catch-up momentum, improving labor markets, and fiscal policy support, while weaker U.S. and global growth and tighter financial conditions were key drag factors; it also noted broadly neutral fiscal policy and untargeted subsidies to offset cost-of-living pressures.","locator":"lines 241-255","source_type":"IGO","source_confidence":"high","source_confidence_reason":"Independent Article IV surveillance with explicit macro attribution, policy description, and contemporaneous assessment.","final_evidence_use":"final_evidence","period_fit":"Directly within the target year.","ruler_attribution":"Mostly attributable to AMLO's administration in combination with external shocks and inherited macro frameworks; the IMF explicitly separates policy support from external drag.","contrary_evidence":["The IMF does not isolate AMLO-only causal shares, and some recovery drivers were inherited or external."],"lenses":["8B.7","8B.9","8B.10"]}

- IMF’s Flexible Credit Line review reinforces that Mexico still rested on strong inherited frameworks while facing external turbulence.
SOURCE_CLAIM_JSON: {"title":"Mexico: Review Under the Flexible Credit Line Arrangement-Press Release; and Staff Report","publisher":"International Monetary Fund","publication_date":"2022-11-17","url":"https://www.elibrary.imf.org/view/journals/002/2022/347/article-A001-en.xml","claim":"The IMF said Mexico qualified for the Flexible Credit Line because of very strong macroeconomic policies and institutional policy frameworks, while also warning that a more turbulent external environment and rising external risks were complicating the recovery.","locator":"summary/abstract and opening context in the IMF review","source_type":"IGO","source_confidence":"high","source_confidence_reason":"Independent IMF review that explicitly links resilience to policy frameworks and notes external-risk pressure.","final_evidence_use":"final_evidence","period_fit":"Directly within 2022.","ruler_attribution":"This mostly reflects Mexico's institutional macro framework, some of which predated AMLO; the review is useful mainly for separating inherited resilience from AMLO-era policy choices.","contrary_evidence":["Because the framework predates AMLO in part, this source limits how much credit can be assigned to 2022 ruler choices alone."],"lenses":["8B.7","8B.9","8B.10"]}

**Gap Resolution**
- Independent outcome audits for flagship programs: partly resolved.
- Attribution versus inherited conditions and external shocks: partly resolved.

**What Still Remains**
- IMSS-Bienestar still leans more on rollout and self-reporting than on independent post-launch outcome audits.
- AIFA and Dos Bocas now have better execution evidence, but durable performance after launch remains thin.
- The causal split between AMLO choices, inherited macro frameworks, and global shocks is clearer than before, but still not fully recoverable.

**Blockers**
- Direct ASF index pages were intermittently slow or timed out, so I used searchable coverage that quotes the audit findings.
- Some Reuters-native pages were not directly fetchable, so I used the Reuters copies hosted by Investing/Infobae where the Reuters text was fully visible.
- I did not find a clean independent 2022 audit of IMSS-Bienestar outcomes that was stronger than the rollout and staffing evidence already in the index.
